dream: The air grew so thick it pressed against the dot until it became a solid lump. The wedge, tired and thin, slid sideways, dragging the wide anchor through the soft floor. I pressed the bush down until its triangle of leaves squashed into nothingness. Then the rough roof came down, heavy and uneven, biting the slip while the card boiled hot and the wide anchor drifted, looking lazy under a weight that had no name.
